summary: Add explicit native retry for failed terminal mission runs. Retry creates a new run using the latest published revision by default, or the source's current revision with --same-revision, retaining exact resolved inputs and workspace. All steps and the program restart from the top; source status, generation and execution history remain unchanged. Run views, mission summaries and missions show expose bidirectional retry links.

replay.detail: Append-only mission-run.retry-linked claims on source and retry subjects preserve lineage and the optional reason. Replaying these claims restores retry_of and retried_by without changing source execution state. Exact-key request replay returns the existing retry instead of creating another run.

schema.detail: Register system-only mission-run.retry-linked with required source and retry mission-run references and optional reason. Add optional retry_of and retried_by to public mission run summaries and generated clients. No local storage-version change or destructive data rewrite.

rules.detail: The claim registry gains mission-run.retry-linked, changing its compatibility digest. Retry uses ordinary run-start authority for a person or the owning agent; it does not grant run-revision authority or change existing start permissions.

compatibility.detail: Upgrade participating members before writing retry-link claims because the registry digest changes. Upgrade the daemon before using the new CLI retry command and POST /v1/mission-runs/{run}/retry route. New clients accept summaries without retry fields from older daemons; older tolerant readers ignore the additive fields. No automatic supersession is introduced.

downtime.detail: No data migration or automatic restart of existing runs. Retry is an explicit operation.

manual.detail: Use missions retry RUN --as ACTOR after a failed run becomes terminal. Select --same-revision explicitly to repeat the source revision. Latest-revision input incompatibility refuses with both revisions and a reason, never falling back. Steps must be idempotent against existing workspace and external effects because the entire run restarts.

recovery.detail: Retry does not roll back prior side effects or erase the failed run. Inspect the new run and its retry_of/retried_by links to recover execution context. Stop writing retry claims before downgrading participating members; retain durable claims and restore a build that recognizes their registry to read lineage.
